v2.note: Prompted by the simulator session finding that dutyKW is NOT vapourFlowTPerH x h_fg(vapourTempC) — it implies 2-7% more condensing flow. The cause is two sensible-cooling terms plus a vent fraction and a wider enthalpy span, not extra vapour, so the excess is heat and not mass. They also found the resistance network could not be closed from what v1 published: fouling, tube wall and conductivity account for 26-36% of 1/U and were absent. No existing value moves.

v1.note: First revision. Answers the six questions asked before the fixture was built rather than across revisions after it.

dutyComposition.whyNotVapourTimesLatentHeat: dutyKW is NOT vapourFlowTPerH x h_fg(vapourTempC). That relation implies a condensing flow 2-7% too large, varying by case. Three effects, pulling in opposite directions: (1) the condensing term is net of the vent fraction, so it uses m_vap x (1 - VENT_FRACTION) and is 3% SMALLER; (2) it subcools to the distillate outlet temperature rather than to the vapour temperature, so the enthalpy span is h_vap(T_vap) - h_liq(T_distOut), WIDER than h_fg(T_vap); (3) two sensible terms add heat from the distillate cascade and the first-effect steam condensate.
dutyComposition.theExcessIsHeatNotVapour: CRITICAL for a coupled model. The 2-7% excess is NOT additional condensing flow. Both sensible terms cool streams that arrive as LIQUID — already condensed upstream — so treating the excess as extra vapour would add mass that is not there. Take the condensing load from dutyBreakdownKW.condensing, and the sensible terms as what they are.
dutyComposition.condensateCoolingIsZeroHere: condensateCooling is 0.0 kW in every case on this grid, because first-effect steam condensate is not routed to the final condenser in these configurations. It is a real term in the model, not a placeholder — do not assume it stays zero for a different condensate extraction setting.

seawaterOutletRule.designBasis: Confirmed by the domain user 2026-08-04: 5 K is the MED default and a designer raises it to 7 or 8 K as the duty requires. It is a DESIGN CHOICE, not a physical constant and not a derived quantity — which is why it is an optional input rather than a computed one. Cases on this grid span 5 K (cond-01..05), 7 K (cond-07) and 8 K (cond-06).
seawaterOutletRule.isADefaultNotAConstant: v1 of this fixture left condenserSWOutlet unset in every case, so the rise was 5.00 K everywhere and a settable input looked like a constant. Seawater FLOW is derived from it, not independent: m_sw = Q / (cp_sw x dT_sw). A dynamic model that varies cooling water flow freely has left the regime these cases describe — here the flow follows from the duty and the chosen rise.
seawaterOutletRule.cascadeEffect: MEASURED, and it is the dominant consequence of this input. Raising the rise from 5 to 8 K moves the last effect from 39.63 to 42.64 °C and its pressure from 66.7 to 78.8 mbar, which COMPRESSES the available cascade from 19.43 to 16.92 K and costs 22% MORE evaporator area (507.6 to 619.4 m2). Condenser duty moves only 0.6%. A cold-end choice whose largest effect is three steps upstream, in a different piece of equipment.
seawaterOutletRule.alsoSetsTheCascade: T_sw,out feeds the last-effect vapour temperature via + condenserApproach, so it moves the whole temperature cascade, not just the condenser. That is why cond-04 (widened approach) differs from cond-06 (raised outlet) despite both changing the cold end.

resistanceNetwork.note: The constants needed to CLOSE 1/U from the two film coefficients. Without them a U disagreement can be seen but not attributed, and gateGuidance asks for exactly that attribution. These account for roughly 26-36% of 1/U, so they are not a rounding term.
resistanceNetwork.relation: 1/U = 1/h_shell + R_f,shell + (OD x ln(OD/ID))/(2 x k_wall) + R_f,tube x (OD/ID) + (1/h_tube) x (OD/ID)
resistanceNetwork.correction: v3 PUBLISHED THE WRONG TUBE CONSTANTS. It gave a 1.0 mm wall and k = 138 W/(m·K) — the EVAPORATOR defaults (Al 5052) — while condenser tubes are 17 x 0.4 mm TITANIUM with k = 21. A consumer closing the network from those figures computes U about 2.3% low, in one direction, which is what the simulator session measured (1.8-3.7%). Their observation that referring the tube-side coefficient to the mean diameter narrowed the gap was a real signal pointing at the right term: the wrong wall thickness also gives the wrong OD/ID referral ratio (1.133 against 1.049), and a mean-diameter referral partly cancels it. The constants are now taken PER CASE from the calculator result rather than assumed, so they cannot drift again.
resistanceNetwork.perCaseConstants: tubeWallThicknessMm, tubeConductivityWmK and tubeMaterial are on each case under expected, not here — they are outputs of the design, not fixture-level constants.
resistanceNetwork.note_whichSideIsWhich: In the CONDENSER seawater is tube-side and condensing distillate is shell-side, so R_f,tube is the seawater value and R_f,shell the distillate one. In a MED EFFECT it is the other way round — steam condenses inside the tubes and brine sprays outside. The asymmetry is the geometry, not an inconsistency.

workflow.flashChamberAndCondenserAreSeparate: BY DESIGN, not a gap. A flash chamber directly connected to a condenser is rare in practice, so Vapour Toolbox keeps them as separate calculators and the engineer links them by hand through the saturation temperature: choose the operating pressure, read the saturation temperature, size the chamber with flashChamberCalculator, then take the vapour flow and temperature into heatDutyCalculator and heatExchangerSizing as a latent duty. heatExchangerSizing handles sensible, latent or combined duty and is used for MED condensers and preheaters.
workflow.whatThatMeansForACoupledModel: The flash chamber takes its operating pressure as an INPUT; it is not derived from a condenser energy balance. A coupled model where flash pressure emerges from condensation is doing something neither reference here can check — that is a difference in what the tools are for, not a defect in these. Correctness there rests on conservation and the model's own invariants, and a run report should say so.

overallU.shellSideCorrelation: Nusselt film condensation, with Kern row correction and an NCG degradation factor
overallU.capNote: There is NO cap on the condenser U. This differs from the evaporator, which is capped at MED_EVAPORATOR_DESIGN_U_WM2K (3,100 W/m²·K) and reports `overallHTCSource` as correlated / design-cap / user-override. `sizeCondensingHX` has no such limit, so the reported U is always the correlated value and "which was used" has one answer here.

lmtdConvention.note: Counterflow, with the hot side ISOTHERMAL (hotInlet = hotOutlet = vapour temperature), so dT1 = T_vap - T_sw,out and dT2 = T_vap - T_sw,in. The F-factor branch in calculateLMTD only fires for CROSSFLOW and SHELL_AND_TUBE; COUNTER leaves it at 1.0.
lmtdConvention.whyFactorOneIsCorrect: With an isothermal hot side the two temperature differences are the same PAIR under counterflow and parallel flow — only their order swaps — and LMTD is symmetric in that pair. So the arrangement does not change the answer and F = 1 is correct rather than an omission. Stated because an unexplained F = 1 is exactly the kind of thing that becomes a 2% mystery for three revisions.

filmCoefficients.note: tubeSideHTC and shellSideHTC are given per case, never only as a combined U. A single U can be compared; two coefficients can be diagnosed. This is the same reason the vacuum fixture reports dry NCG and vapour separately rather than one total.

offDesign.note: U IS A POINT, NOT A CURVE. `sizeCondensingHX` takes a design tube velocity (1.8 m/s for the condenser) and iterates the tube count until the actual velocity matches, then computes U at that velocity. There is no U(load) or U(velocity) relation anywhere in this calculator, and interpolating these five cases into one would be inventing a shape the model does not have — the same error as building an ejector capacity curve out of a single sizing point.
offDesign.whatCanBeDoneInstead: The tube-side coefficient IS a velocity relation: Dittus-Boelter gives Nu ∝ Re^0.8, so h_tube ∝ v^0.8 at fixed properties. A dynamic model can scale h_tube off-design from the reported design-point value and re-form U with the shell side held, which is defensible. The shell side has no equivalent scaling here: Nusselt condensation depends on the film and the row count, not on a load parameter this calculator varies.

knownLimitations.hotwellHoldup: ABSENT. The hotwell exists as a concept — gross condensate is extracted from it — but no volume, level or inventory is modelled anywhere. Same reason MED effects have no liquid holdup: there is no liquid inventory model, only a shipping-weight fill allowance used for operating weight.
knownLimitations.ventCondenser: NOT MODELLED, and this is a match rather than a gap. `finalCondenserModel` removes a flat VENT_FRACTION = 0.03 of the vapour to vacuum and models nothing between the vessel and the vacuum system — no vent condenser, no separate coolant. A coupled model drawing its vent at vessel conditions with nothing in between is doing the same thing, so `ventGasTemperature` from the vacuum fixture applies as-is.
knownLimitations.metalMass: DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS FIXTURE. The condenser mass is `designArea x 50 kg/m²`, a budgetary allowance assuming titanium, with no geometry behind it — despite full tube geometry being available on this very object. A fixture is precisely where a cost allowance would be read as a thermal mass, so it is excluded rather than caveated. Condenser thermal mass is a §4.3 calibration parameter with no prior.
knownLimitations.designMarginInArea: designAreaM2 carries the design margin; requiredAreaM2 does not. Gate against requiredArea when checking the heat transfer, and against designArea only when checking the sizing decision.

gateGuidance.order: Gate on duty and LMTD first, then the two film coefficients, then U, then required area. A U mismatch with both coefficients matching is a resistance-network difference; a coefficient mismatch is a correlation difference. Checking U alone cannot separate them.
gateGuidance.whatNotToGate: Do not gate on designArea without accounting for the design margin, on tube count (a selection, not a physical result), or on anything off-design.

cases.note: Colder seawater. Raises LMTD at fixed duty, so area falls — the cleanest single-variable check on the LMTD convention.
Warmer seawater. The opposite direction, and the one that squeezes LMTD toward the approach.
Wider condenser approach at the base seawater temperature — moves the seawater outlet independently of the inlet.
Fewer effects, so more vapour reaches the condenser: a materially larger duty on the same geometry basis.
